Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 69, verses 1–3:

(p-٥٩١٠) In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Surah al-Haqqah

Makkiyyah (revealed in Makkah). Its number of verses is fifty-one.

(p-٥٩١١) In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

On the interpretation (ta'wil) of His saying, Exalted is He:

[1–3] ﴿The Inevitable Reality.﴾ ﴿What is the Inevitable Reality?﴾ ﴿And what will make you know what the Inevitable Reality is?﴾

﴿al-Haqqah﴾ means: the Hour (al-sa'ah), the Inevitable Reality, in which matters become established (tahiqqu) and in which the recompense for deeds becomes due (yajibu). It is from their saying: "haqqa 'alayhi al-shay'," meaning it became due for him, when it became obligatory.

His saying: ﴿ma al-Haqqah﴾ (what is the Inevitable Reality?) is the placing of the apparent noun in the place of the pronoun, to magnify its matter and to exalt its terror. ﴿Wa ma adraka ma al-Haqqah﴾ (And what will make you know what the Inevitable Reality is?). Some of them said: it is among the subtle customs of the Arabs in their discourse: when they wish to arouse the addressee's eagerness to know a thing and to understand it, they bring a general statement followed by a detailed one, meaning: what has informed the addressee of what it is? This is an emphasis on magnifying its matter, until it seems to have gone out of the range of the addressee's knowledge, in the sense that: its great matter and the attributes it comprises are such that the understanding of none of the addressees has reached them, nor the knowledge of any of the hearers attained them, nor has their imagination grasped them. However its state is conceived, it lies beyond that and is greater. From this it is known that the interrogative is a metonymy (kinayah) for its necessary implication, namely that it is not known, that the understanding of no abode reaches it, and that thoughts do not attain it.

The interpretation of His words, may He be exalted:

[4–8] ﴿Thamud and 'Ad denied the Striking Calamity.﴾ ﴿As for Thamud, they were destroyed by the Overwhelming Blast.﴾ [al-Haqqah: 5] ﴿As for 'Ad, they were destroyed by a furious, roaring wind.﴾ [al-Haqqah: 6] (p-5912) ﴿He subjected it against them for seven nights and eight days, in succession, so you could see the people lying prostrate in it as though they were trunks of hollow palm trees.﴾ [al-Haqqah: 7] ﴿So do you see any remnant of them?﴾ [al-Haqqah: 8]

﴿Thamud and 'Ad denied the Striking Calamity﴾: that is, the Hour that strikes people with its terrors and its sudden assault upon them.

Al-Zamakhshari said: The phrase was placed in the position of a pronoun to indicate the meaning of "striking" in al-Haqqah, as an increase in describing its severity. When he mentioned it and magnified it, he followed the mention of it with mention of those who denied it and what befell them because of their denial, as a reminder to the people of Makkah and a warning to them about the consequence of their denial. ﴿As for Thamud﴾ [al-Haqqah: 5], they were the people of Salih, peace be upon him. ﴿They were destroyed by the Overwhelming Blast﴾ [al-Haqqah: 5], that is, by the event that exceeds the limit in severity, or by their transgression. "Al-Taghiyah" is a verbal noun (masdar) like "al-'afiyah." ﴿As for 'Ad﴾ [al-Haqqah: 6], they were the people of Hud, peace be upon him. ﴿They were destroyed by a furious wind﴾ [al-Haqqah: 6], that is, a wind of intense gusting and cold. ﴿Roaring﴾ [al-Haqqah: 6], that is, exceeding the known limit in blowing and coldness.

﴿He subjected it﴾ [al-Haqqah: 7], that is, He let it loose ﴿against them for seven nights and eight days, in succession﴾ [al-Haqqah: 7], that is, consecutive, from "hasamtu al-dabbah," when you continue cauterizing an animal's wound one after another. He likened the continuity of the uprooting wind to the continuity of the cauterizing iron that cuts off a disease. Or its meaning is: ill-omened, for it cut off and uprooted every good; or cutting, for it severed their roots. This is on the basis that "husuman" [al-Haqqah: 7] is the plural of "hasim," like "shuhud" and "qu'ud." If it is a verbal noun, then its accusative case is governed by an implied verb, meaning "it cuts off in cutting off," or it is an object of purpose (maf'ul lahu), meaning "He subjected it against them for cutting off (husum), that is, uprooting." It has been said that those days are the days of "al-'ajuz" (the final days of winter). The common people call it "al-'ajuz," which is the time that falls at the end (ajz) of winter, that is, its last part.

﴿So you could see the people lying prostrate in it﴾ [al-Haqqah: 7], that is, dead, the plural of "sari'" (a fallen one), ﴿as though they were trunks of hollow palm trees﴾ [al-Haqqah: 7], that is, fallen, uprooted from their bases, like the verse:

﴿As though they were trunks of uprooted palm trees﴾ [al-Qamar: 20].

﴿So do you see any remnant of them?﴾ [al-Haqqah: 8], that is, any survival, or a surviving soul, or a remnant.

The explanation of His saying, exalted is He:

[9–12] ﴿And Pharaoh came, and those before him, and the overturned cities with sin﴾ ﴿and they disobeyed the messenger of their Lord, so He seized them with a seizing overwhelming﴾ [al-Haqqah: 10] ﴿Indeed, when the water overflowed, We carried you in the sailing vessel﴾ [al-Haqqah: 11] ﴿That We might make it for you a reminder, and that a retaining ear might retain it﴾ [al-Haqqah: 12]

﴿And Pharaoh came, and those before him﴾: that is, from the disbelieving nations, such as the people of Noah, ʿAd and Thamud. ﴿And the overturned cities﴾: these are the towns of the people of Lot. ﴿With sin﴾: that is, with error, or with sinful deeds, by way of metonymy in the attribution. ﴿And they disobeyed the messenger of their Lord, so He seized them with a seizing﴾ [al-Haqqah: 10]: that is, exceeding in severity.

﴿Indeed, when the water overflowed﴾ [al-Haqqah: 11]: that is, it increased and exceeded its known limit, because of the persistence of the people of Noah in disbelief and sins, and their denial of him, peace be upon him. ﴿We carried you in the sailing vessel﴾ [al-Haqqah: 11]: that is, the ship that runs upon the water.

Ibn Jarir said: He addressed those among whom the Qur'an was revealed, and He carried their forefathers, Noah and his offspring; for those who were addressed by this are the descendants of those who were carried in the vessel. So the carrying of those who were carried in it from among the forefathers is a carrying of their descendants. ﴿That We might make it﴾ [al-Haqqah: 12]: that is, that act, which is the salvation of the believers and the drowning of the disbelievers, ﴿for you a reminder﴾ [al-Haqqah: 12]: that is, a sign and a lesson by which you remember the truth of His promise to help His messengers and to destroy their enemies.

﴿And a retaining ear might retain it﴾ [al-Haqqah: 12]: that is, preserve it. ﴿A retaining ear﴾ [al-Haqqah: 12]: that is, one that holds onto what it has heard of Allah, reflecting upon it.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 69, verse 38–43:

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:

[38–43] ﴿So I swear by what you see﴾ ﴿and what you do not see﴾ [al-Haqqah: 39] ﴿Indeed, it is the word of a noble Messenger﴾ [al-Haqqah: 40] ﴿And it is not the word of a poet; little do you believe﴾ [al-Haqqah: 41] ﴿Nor the word of a soothsayer; little do you remember﴾ [al-Haqqah: 42] ﴿It is a revelation from the Lord of the worlds﴾ [al-Haqqah: 43]

﴿So I swear by what you see﴾ ﴿and what you do not see﴾ [al-Haqqah: 39]: that is, by the things that are witnessed and by the things that are unseen. This oath, as al-Razi said, encompasses all things in their entirety, since they do not fall outside two categories: that which is seen and that which is not seen. It thus includes the Creator and the creation, this world and the Hereafter, the upper world and the lower world, and so on. The discussion of the phrase "I swear not" (lā uqsimu) has already been covered in Surat al-Waqi'ah, so refer back to it.

﴿Indeed, it﴾ [al-Haqqah: 40], that is, the Qur'an, ﴿is the word of a noble Messenger﴾ [al-Haqqah: 40], namely Muhammad (ﷺ), who conveys it from Allah, exalted is He, because a messenger does not convey from himself.

﴿And it is not the word of a poet﴾ [al-Haqqah: 41], that is, as you claim. For between its style and its realities, and between the meter of poetry and its imaginings, lies the distance of the two easts.

﴿Little do you believe﴾ [al-Haqqah: 41]: you affirm what has manifested its truthfulness and proof only out of obstinacy and arrogance. The word "little" (qalīlan) is a metaphor for negation and non-existence. "Qalīlan" is in the accusative as an attribute of a verbal noun (maṣdar) or of an implied time, that is, "belief" (īmānan) and "time" (zamānan). The governing element is "tu'minūna" or "tadhakkarūna," and "mā" is superfluous (zā'idah). This is what Ibn 'Adil said, while Ibn 'Atiyyah said: it is possible that it is negating and verbal (maṣdariyyah).

﴿Nor the word of a soothsayer﴾ [al-Haqqah: 42], that is, as you assert in another claim, that it is from the rhymed prose (saj') of soothsayers (kuhhān).

﴿Little do you remember﴾ [al-Haqqah: 42]: that is, you take heed and reflect. It has been said: He negated belief in the first and remembrance in the second, because the Qur'an's lack of resemblance to poetry is a clear matter that none denies except an obstinate one. Thus there is no excuse for the one who says it in abandoning belief, and he is more disbelieving than a donkey. As for its difference from soothsaying, it depends upon some reflection, because the soothsayer takes a fee, answers whatever he is asked about, forces rhymed prose, and lies much, even if it is confused for fools by his reports of some unseen matters in prose speech. So reflect.

﴿A revelation﴾ [al-Haqqah: 43], that is, it is a revelation ﴿from the Lord of the worlds﴾ [al-Haqqah: 43], that is, from the One who nurtured them with various kinds of blessings, among which is that He sent it down and revealed it so that they might be guided by it to the paths of happiness and the methods of success.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 69, verses 44–47:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[44–47] ﴿And if he had falsely attributed to Us some sayings﴾ ﴿We would have seized him by the right hand﴾ [al-Haqqah: 45] ﴿Then We would have severed from him the aorta﴾ [al-Haqqah: 46] ﴿And not one of you could have prevented Us from him﴾ [al-Haqqah: 47]

﴿And if he had falsely attributed to Us some sayings﴾: that is, if he had fabricated against Us. He called lying "taqawwul" (fabricating speech) because it is speech that is contrived, as the form of the verb tafa''ala (taf'ul) indicates. As for ﴿al-aqawil﴾ (the sayings), it is either the plural of qawl (saying) in an irregular manner, or the plural of a plural, like al-a'na'im, the plural of aqwal and an'am. It was said: calling the fabricated sayings "aqawil" is a belittling of them, as though it were the plural of uf'ula from qawl, like al-ada-hik (the laughing-stocks).

﴿We would have seized him by the right hand﴾ [al-Haqqah: 45] ﴿Then We would have severed from him the aorta﴾ [al-Haqqah: 46]. Ibn Jarir said: that is, We would have seized him with Our power and might, then We would have severed from him the aorta of the heart. He only means by this that He would hasten to punish him and not delay it. It has also been said that the meaning of His saying ﴿We would have seized him by the right hand﴾ [al-Haqqah: 45] is: We would have taken him by his right hand from before him. He said: this is only like the saying of a ruler when he wants to belittle one of those before him to one of his helpers: "Take him by his hand and set him up, and do such-and-such to him." They said: likewise the meaning of His saying ﴿We would have seized him by the right hand﴾ [al-Haqqah: 45] is: We would have humiliated him, like one who does to the one whose condition we have described. End.

Al-Zamakhshari said: The meaning is: if he claimed something of Us that We had not said, We would have killed him by execution, as kings do with one who lies against them, treating him with anger and vengeance. So he depicted killing by execution in its form so that it would be more dreadful: that he is taken by his hand and his neck is struck. The right hand was singled out over the left, because when the killer wants to strike the back of the neck, he seizes him by his left hand, and when he wants to strike the neck and cut it with the sword, which is more severe on the one being executed because of his looking at the sword, he seizes him by his right hand. So the meaning of ﴿We would have seized him by the right hand﴾ [al-Haqqah: 45] is: We would have seized him by his right hand, just as His saying ﴿We would have severed from him the aorta﴾ [al-Haqqah: 46] means: We would have severed his aorta. This is clear. End.

What al-Zamakhshari established is more eloquent in conveying the intended meaning, which is the explanation of punishment with the most severe punishment. For according to the first view, the depiction, the detail and the summary are lost, because His saying ﴿by the right hand﴾ [al-Haqqah: 45] after ﴿We would have seized him﴾ [al-Haqqah: 45] is an explanation after ambiguity, and His saying "from him" becomes superfluous without benefit, and metaphor is employed without benefit as well, as in al-Inayah.

﴿And not one of you could have prevented Us from him﴾ [al-Haqqah: 47]: that is, there is none among you who could hold Us back from him or come between Us and his punishment, if he had fabricated against Us.

﴿So glorify the name of your Lord, the Mighty﴾ [al-Haqqah: 52], i.e., remain constant in remembering His name, persevere in calling to Him alone and to what He has revealed to you. So the final outcome belongs to you and to those believers who follow you.
